app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

insights: A single payment pod (payment-6c5f448889-rgh86) is Running in the astronomy-shop namespace (no pod crash or restart evidence found).

Pod logs contain repeated WARN entries: "Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold", repeatedly over the observed time window — authentication failures are occurring on every charge attempt.

Stack traces in the log entries point to application code paths (module.exports.charge in charge.js and chargeServiceHandler in index.js), showing the error originates in the payment charge flow within the service.

The failure pattern is persistent and frequent (many repeated messages), indicating a bad/expired/rotated application credential rather than an intermittent network error or transient downstream outage.

Correlated evidence (pod present and running + repeated 'Invalid token' errors) supports the root cause: the payment service is using an invalid/expired/rotated API token (app-level credential), causing the payment provider to reject charge requests.
No Kubernetes-level resource failures or misconfigurations were identified in this investigation; the issue is an application credential/authentication problem with the payment integration.

final_report.root_cause: The payment Service port was named non-protocol-specifically (`tcp-service`), causing Envoy (frontend-proxy) to treat the backend as generic TCP rather than HTTP. As a result HTTP header semantics (the payment auth token header) were not preserved/forwarded to the payment service. The payment service therefore attempted charges with a missing/invalid token and the external payment provider rejected the requests (logged as "Invalid token"). This combination (service port naming + baked-in Envoy behavior) produced persistent payment failures during checkout.

Invalid token."; multiple traceIDs recorded. 2) Logs from the single running payment pod (payment-6c5f448889-rgh86) show repeated WARN entries and stack traces from the charge flow: "Payment request failed. Invalid token." 3) checkout Deployment is configured to call payment:8080 (PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080) and payment Service exposes targetPort 8080 -> endpoints 10.244.1.13:8080, confirming connectivity. 4) payment Service port is named "tcp-service" (not an HTTP/gRPC protocol name), and frontend-proxy has no mounted Envoy config (config baked into image), indicating Envoy likely used protocol detection and treated the backend as TCP so HTTP headers (token) were not applied/preserved. 5) payment Deployment does not reference a Kubernetes Secret or mounted token, suggesting the token should arrive via request headers rather than from a pod secret—consistent with header loss explaining the failures.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority 1 (epicenter): Examined payment service pods and logs — found a single running payment pod with repeated "Invalid token" errors, indicating authentication failures during charge attempts. Priority 2 (checkout->payment): Verified checkout's PAYMENT_ADDR (payment:8080) matches payment Service ClusterIP/endpoint — no host/port mismatch. Priority 3 (frontend-proxy->payment): Inspected payment Service port name and frontend-proxy deployment — service port named "tcp-service" and Envoy config baked into image; concluded Envoy likely treated backend as TCP and did not apply HTTP header semantics, causing token header loss. Priority 4 (secrets): Checked payment deployment for Secret references — none found, so a Kubernetes Secret rotation is unlikely. Correlated findings create a causal chain: service port naming caused protocol mismatch in Envoy -> token header not forwarded -> payment service lacked valid token and external payment provider rejected charges -> checkout failures logged as "Invalid token." Immediate remediation is to change the payment Service port name to an HTTP protocol name (e.g., "http" or "http-payment"), which will allow Envoy to apply HTTP semantics and preserve headers; if Envoy config/image still misdetects, update Envoy config or restart/redeploy frontend-proxy to pick up protocol-aware routing.
